roadmap.why_it_matters: Every professional developer must know how to track code changes and collaborate using Git.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Basic Git workflow: init, add, commit, push, and creating a GitHub repository.
roadmap.task: Install Git, create a GitHub account, initialize a repository locally, and push your first Python script to GitHub.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Commit a change to your README file and push it to GitHub using only the command line.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Writing reusable and modular code is the foundation of clean software development.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Function definition, parameters, return values, and the difference between global and local scope.
roadmap.task: Write a Python script with functions to calculate the area of various shapes based on input parameters.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Create a function that accepts a list of numbers and returns only the even ones.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Data structures like lists and dictionaries are used to manage data in almost every software application.
roadmap.what_to_learn: List comprehensions, dictionary key-value pairing, nested lists, and basic dictionary methods.
roadmap.task: Build a simple console-based phonebook dictionary that allows users to add, search, and delete contacts.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Use a list comprehension to double all elements in a numeric list in a single line of code.

roadmap.why_it_matters: OOP is the dominant programming paradigm used in enterprise software development.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Classes, objects, the __init__ method, and class attributes vs instance attributes.
roadmap.task: Create a 'Car' class with attributes like brand, model, and year, and instantiate three different objects.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Add a method 'drive()' to your Car class that prints 'The [brand] is driving!'.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Inheritance prevents code duplication by allowing classes to inherit properties from parent classes.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Parent vs child classes, super() function, and overriding parent methods.
roadmap.task: Create an 'ElectricCar' child class that inherits from the 'Car' class and adds a 'battery_size' attribute.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Override the 'drive()' method in ElectricCar to print 'The [brand] is driving silently!'.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Encapsulation protects class data from unauthorized external access, boosting software security.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Private and protected attributes (double underscores) and getter/setter methods.
roadmap.task: Modify your Car class to make the 'mileage' attribute private, and write a getter and setter method for it.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Attempt to access the private attribute directly from outside the class and handle the error.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Robust software must gracefully handle errors without crashing completely.
roadmap.what_to_learn: try, except, else, and finally blocks, and catching specific exceptions (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError).
roadmap.task: Write a program that prompts the user for two numbers, divides them, and safely handles ZeroDivisionError.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Create a try-except block that handles a missing file error (FileNotFoundError).

roadmap.why_it_matters: Software developers must write efficient algorithms to handle large-scale user data.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Understanding O(1), O(N), and O(N^2) complexity and how loops affect execution speed.
roadmap.task: Analyze three simple code snippets containing loops and write down their theoretical Big O runtimes.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Identify a piece of code with an O(N^2) runtime and explain why it is slow.

roadmap.why_it_matters: These sequential data structures form the backbones of functions like undo buttons and print queues.
roadmap.what_to_learn: LIFO (Last In First Out) for Stacks and FIFO (First In First Out) for Queues using Python lists/collections.deque.
roadmap.task: Implement a Stack class using a Python list with custom push() and pop() methods.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Use a list as a Stack to reverse the characters of a given string.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Recursion is a key coding pattern for solving complex problems by dividing them into simpler sub-problems.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Base cases, recursive cases, and call stacks.
roadmap.task: Write a recursive function to calculate the factorial of a given positive integer.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Write a recursive function to calculate the N-th number in the Fibonacci sequence.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Binary search reduces search time from O(N) to O(log N), vital for fast data retrieval.
roadmap.what_to_learn: The divide-and-conquer strategy on a sorted list.
roadmap.task: Implement the classic Binary Search algorithm in Python to find an index of a target value in a sorted list.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Compare the execution steps of Linear Search vs Binary Search on a list of size 100.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Understanding how the internet handles requests is critical for any backend or web developer.
roadmap.what_to_learn: The client-server model, HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), and status codes.
roadmap.task: Sketch a simple diagram illustrating how a web browser retrieves a page from a Python backend server.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Explain the difference between a GET request and a POST request in your own words.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Software apps store user data, preferences, and content inside structured databases.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Relational databases, tables, columns, data types, primary keys, and basic SELECT queries.
roadmap.task: Write out a design schema (table names and column names) for a 'Users' database on paper.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Write a conceptual SQL query to fetch a user with an email 'hema@example.com'.

roadmap.why_it_matters: To become a developer, you must know how to insert and fetch filtered datasets.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Filtering data with WHERE, sorting with ORDER BY, and writing INSERT statements.
roadmap.task: Use an online sandbox (like SQLBolt) to complete interactive exercises on filtering rows.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Write an INSERT statement to add a new employee named 'Alice' to an 'employees' table.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Python has built-in SQLite support, allowing you to create local database-driven applications easily.
roadmap.what_to_learn: The 'sqlite3' module, connecting to a database, executing queries, and committing changes.
roadmap.task: Write a Python script that creates a local SQLite database table called 'tasks' and inserts two items.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Write Python code to select all tasks from the database and print them to the console.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework perfect for beginners looking to build web APIs and projects.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Flask installation, pip environments, and basic routing.
roadmap.task: Set up a virtual environment, install Flask, and write a 'Hello World' Flask application.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Add a secondary route '/about' that returns your name and target role when visited in the browser.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Web pages require dynamic paths to load specific profiles, posts, or dynamic products.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Route variables, data conversion types in routes (<int:id>).
roadmap.task: Create a route `/user/<username>` in your Flask app that prints a customized welcome message for that user.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Create a route `/square/<int:num>` that calculates and returns the square of the input number.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Separating business logic (Python) from UI logic (HTML) keeps code clean and maintainable.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Rendering templates using render_template(), template variables, and loop structures inside HTML.
roadmap.task: Create a simple HTML file index.html inside a 'templates' folder and serve it dynamically using Flask.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Pass a list of hobbies from your Python code and list them using a Jinja2 for-loop in your HTML.

roadmap.topic: Flask Forms and Handling POST Requests
roadmap.why_it_matters: Web forms allow users to submit dynamic input, register accounts, or post content.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Handling HTTP POST requests, reading form fields via request.form.
roadmap.task: Build an HTML form with an input text box, configure Flask to handle its POST action, and print the input.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Validate that the form submission is not empty before returning the response.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Planning architecture before coding saves development hours and ensures project logical sense.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Software requirements gathering and basic system/database flow diagramming.
roadmap.task: Draft a plan for a basic SQLite-backed Task Manager (Tasks: ID, Title, Status). Draw the app flow.
roadmap.mini_challenge: List 3 basic functionalities of your upcoming web project (e.g., View Tasks, Add Task, Delete Task).

roadmap.why_it_matters: Setting up the database structure is the first tangible step to storing actual user data.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Executing CREATE TABLE via python, setting up initial parameters.
roadmap.task: Write an initialization script `init_db.py` to set up your 'tasks' table using Python sqlite3.
roadmap.mini_challenge: Run the setup file and verify the presence of 'database.db' in your project directory.

roadmap.why_it_matters: Reading data from the storage engine is the most fundamental database read operation.
roadmap.what_to_learn: Querying SQLite using SELECT inside Flask endpoints, passing lists to dynamic Jinja layouts.
